sentences.text: :JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 01052016 at about 4.45 p.m., when the Petitioner was riding a three wheeler motor cycle bearing No.AP 03AL1328 from Chittoor towards Bengaluru side and when he reached Sruthi Milk diary, at that time, a lorry bearing Regn.No.TN28AH8487 driven by its driver came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Petitioner's three wheeler motor cycle and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Government Hospital, Chittoor for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to CMC Hospital, Vellor, wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient.
He has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as MeeSeva in Chittoor and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.

Due to the accident,
he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending lorry and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the lorry and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent.

Hence,
he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through its counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further contended that, there is a delay in filing the claim petition.
Further, it contended that at the time of alleged accident, the offending vehicle was plied without valid permit and fitness certificate.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.

2 ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 01.05.2016 at about 4.45 p.m. near Sruthi Milk Diary, on BengaluruChittoor road,
Chittooor district, Andhra Pradesh, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of lorry bearing No. TN28AH8487?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
He also examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P12 & P.13 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined a witness as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 01052016 at about 4.45 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing Regn.No.TN28AH8487.
8.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P13.
P.W.1 has re iterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of FIR,
Complaint, Charge sheet, Sketch map, Certificate issued by department of radiology and Wound Certificate.
Ex.P.7 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.8 is the Medical bills, Ex.P.9 is the Driving Licence, Ex.P.10 is the Photographs and Ex.P.11 is the copy of CD.

10 . Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR and Ex.P2 Complaint and Ex.P.2(a) i.e., the translated version of the Complaint shows that on the complaint lodged before Chittoor Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN 28AH8487 for the offences punishable under Sec. 337 of IPC.

Ex.P3 is the Certified copy of the S.Shafiulla vs A.Sundara Rajan on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140695113/
3 Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Chittoor Traffic Police Station has submitted Chargesheet against the driver of the offending lorry for the offences punishable under Sec. 338 of IPC.
Ex.P4 is the Sketch and Ex.P.4(a) is the translated sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn sketch at the spot.
Ex.P5 is the Certificate issued by department of Radiology and Ex.P6 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 is the Discharge Summary of the Petitioner.
11. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.
13. Further, the Respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and he reiterated the Objection statement contentions in his chief affidavit.
In the cross examination, he denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner.
Chargesheet is the material document which was submitted by the driver of the offending Lorry for the alleged accident.

Therefore, having regard to the fact and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurrred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.
14. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
15.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 39 years.
He has produced Driving Licence to prove his age.
As per the Driving Licence i.e. Ex.P.9 the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 11.05.1981.
The accident taken place on 01.05.2016.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 35 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as Mee Seva which is contract with Government of Andhra Pradesh and was earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to show that he was earning Rs.15,000/ p.m.

Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2016, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 9,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:

18. The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling and deformity of left wrist.
2. Swelling over right leg near ankle.
Xray of left wrist reveals fracture of lower end of both bones to radius & Xray of right ankle reveals ulna and fracture of lower end of right tibia.
Further, the Doctor has opined that wounds are grievous in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs. 40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
19. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of  40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
20.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 02.05.2016 to 12.05.2016 at Aashraya Hospitals, Chittoor
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Nagaraj.B.N has also reiterated the same in his evidence.

21. Upon going through Ex.P.7 i.e., the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 02.05.2016 to 12.05.2016 at Aashraya Hospitals, Chittoor i.e., totally for 11 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 11 days.
22. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.19,000/ under this head (@ Rs.9,500/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
23.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of  18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :

sentences.text: The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than  2,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 9 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.8 which is totally amounting to Rs.71,585/.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same is acceptable.
Hence, by rounding of the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.71,600/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
25. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and cannot work as earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

26. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked disability certificate and xray at Ex.P.10.
He assessed total disability of both lower limbs at 18%, left upper limb at 11% and whole body disability at 27%.
27. In the crossexamination PW.2 has stated he has not personally treated the petitioner and he has not issued wound certificate.
Further he admitted that since birth, the Petitioner is suffering from polio.
He has also admitted that the fractures are simple and injuries are healed.
He has denied the suggestion that the whole body disability assessed by him is not due to accidental injuries as the Petitioner already suffering from polio.

28. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 16.

With multiplier of 16, income of Rs.9,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,82,400/ (Rs.9,500/ x 12 =
1,14,000/, Rs.1,14,000/x 16 x 10/100 =1,82,400/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of  1,82,400/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
29.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/
3.

Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance S.Shafiulla vs A.Sundara Rajan on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140695113/
6 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 71,600/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 19,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs. 1,82,400/ Total Rs. 3,71,000/
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,71,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

30. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.TN 28AH8487.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.3,71,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75%
of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,71,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.3,71,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75%
of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
